))
functions.yields: The degrees of freedom absorbed by the Fixed Effects group: G − 1 where G is the FE column's level count over the included sample; 0 when no Fixed Effects row is declared or the FE variable is degenerate (G ≤ 1).
functions.description:
Absorbed_Degrees_Of_Freedom is the one-way FE df correction for the Model Construction sheet: G − 1, where G is the count of distinct Fixed Effects levels among the included rows. Every model with no declared Fixed Effects row (the entire v2.0 shipped surface) returns 0 — the same non-breaking default the [DF_Absorbed] argument threads through the inference chain, so a no-FE model's df, MS-Residual, t, p, CI, and AIC/BIC are bit-identical to before this function existed.

Reuses Dummy_Levels for the level count rather than a fresh UNIQUE/COUNT — the exact same mask-scoped, reference-dropped level set the design matrix would use if the FE column were instead one-hot encoded (which is the algebraic content of 'absorbing' a fixed effect: G−1 degrees of freedom are spent whether they are spent explicitly, as G−1 dummy coefficients, or implicitly, by demeaning). COLUMNS(Dummy_Levels(...)) is exactly G−1 by construction, so this function can never disagree with what an equivalent LSDV fit would report. A degenerate FE variable (every included row shares one level) makes Dummy_Levels return #N/A; this function absorbs that into 0 rather than propagating the error, because a single-level 'group' fixes no group-specific intercept and absorbs no degrees of freedom.

One-way only: a spec with two or more Fixed Effects rows is a visible status-block error (validated elsewhere), so this function reads only the first Fixed Effects row via Fixed_Effects_Column() — two-way absorption (Σ over both dimensions, minus the overlap correction) is deferred to the two-way FE milestone (v2.7+).
functions.plain_language_summary: How many degrees of freedom the Fixed Effects variable soaks up (G−1 groups) — 0 when there's no Fixed Effects row.
functions.notes: One-way FE df correction: G−1 via COLUMNS(Dummy_Levels(...)) on the FE column, 0 when no FE row exists or the FE variable is degenerate. Default 0 keeps every no-FE model bit-identical. Two-way absorption deferred to v2.7+.

functions.name: y_s
functions.formula_display:
=LAMBDA(LET(
    n_c,       COLUMNS(Source_Data),
    fe_active, SUMPRODUCT(N(TAKE(Spec_Role, n_c) = "Fixed Effects")) > 0,
    IF(NOT(fe_active),
       Response_Column(),
       Demean_By(Response_Column(), Fixed_Effects_Column(), Sample_Include())
    )
))
functions.yields: The fit-time Response: Response_Column() unchanged when no Fixed Effects row is declared, or its one-way within-transformed (group-demeaned) form when one is; full height.
functions.description:
y_s is the fit-time Response for the Regression sheet — the v2.1 Fixed Effects counterpart to X_s on the predictor side. With no declared Fixed Effects row it is Response_Column() unchanged (the entire v2.0 shipped surface passes through untouched); with one declared, it is Demean_By(Response_Column(), Fixed_Effects_Column(), Sample_Include()) — the one-way within transformation that lets ordinary OLS on the demeaned data reproduce the LSDV (dummy-per-group) fit without materializing G−1 group dummy columns.

Shipped as a NEW function, deliberately not a replacement of Response_Column() at its existing call sites: Response_Column() keeps its raw-response consumers that are unrelated to this fit (Intercept_Only_Point/S/SE/N, the zero-predictor closed-form branch). The Residual Output table's Y column is repointed to y_s() too, not left raw — under FE the whole row-level table (Y, Predicted Y, Residuals, Hat Diagonal, …) must read as one internally consistent block in the same fit space, or Residuals would visibly fail to match Y − Predicted Y. Only the fit/inference/prediction/residual chain (Coefficients, Predictions, Residuals, and everything built from them) is repointed to y_s() — a caller-side choice, not a change to what Response_Column() means.

The no-FE branch is checked first and returns the exact same object Response_Column() would — not merely a numerically-equal recomputation — so every existing no-FE model is unaffected by construction, the same non-breaking-default property Absorbed_Degrees_Of_Freedom relies on for the df side.
functions.plain_language_summary: The response the model actually fits: unchanged with no Fixed Effects, or with each group's average subtracted out when a Fixed Effects variable is declared.
functions.notes: Fit-time Response: Response_Column() unchanged (no FE), else Demean_By(Response_Column(),Fixed_Effects_Column(),Sample_Include()). New function — the zero-predictor Intercept_Only_* branch stays on raw Response_Column().

functions.name: X_s_Within
functions.formula_display:
=LAMBDA(LET(
    n_c,       COLUMNS(Source_Data),
    fe_active, SUMPRODUCT(N(TAKE(Spec_Role, n_c) = "Fixed Effects")) > 0,
    IF(NOT(fe_active),
       X_s(),
       LET(
           fe,  Fixed_Effects_Column(),
           inc, Sample_Include(),
           BYCOL(X_s(), LAMBDA(col, Demean_By(col, fe, inc)))
       )
    )
))
functions.yields: The fit-time design matrix: X_s() unchanged when no Fixed Effects row is declared, or each of its columns one-way within-transformed (group-demeaned) when one is; full height, same width as X_s().
functions.description:
X_s_Within is the fit-time design matrix for the Regression sheet — the predictor-side counterpart to y_s. With no declared Fixed Effects row it is X_s() unchanged; with one declared, BYCOL demeans every constructed column of X_s() by the Fixed Effects group via Demean_By, reproducing the LSDV fit's coefficients on the non-FE predictors without ever materializing the G−1 group dummy columns an explicit one-hot encoding would require.

Shipped as a NEW function alongside y_s, for the identical reason: X_s() has raw-predictor consumers that must not see demeaned values — the Predictor Summary zone (Pearson_R, Spearman_R, Skewness, Kurtosis, GVIF, Generalized_Tolerance) characterizes each predictor's own distribution, and Constructed_Column_Names() labels columns positionally against X_s(), not X_s_Within(). Only the fit/inference/prediction/residual chain (Coefficients, Predictions, Residuals, Hat_Diagonal, Cooks_Distance, and everything built from them) is repointed to X_s_Within() — repointing which columns those formulas READ, not a change to what X_s() itself returns.

The no-FE branch returns X_s() itself, unchanged, so every existing no-FE model is unaffected by construction — including its error behavior: a zero-predictor spec that makes X_s() itself error propagates through X_s_Within() identically, never masked.
functions.plain_language_summary: The design matrix the model actually fits: unchanged with no Fixed Effects, or with each predictor column's group average subtracted out when a Fixed Effects variable is declared.
functions.notes: Fit-time design matrix: X_s() unchanged (no FE), else each column demeaned by Fixed_Effects_Column() via Demean_By (BYCOL). New function — Predictor Summary and Constructed_Column_Names() stay on raw X_s().

functions.name: Serial_Correlation_Group
functions.formula_display:
=LAMBDA(LET(
    roles, TAKE(Spec_Role, COLUMNS(Source_Data)),
    key, IFS(
        SUMPRODUCT(N(roles = "Fixed Effects")) > 0, "Fixed Effects",
        SUMPRODUCT(N(roles = "Cluster")) > 0, "Cluster",
        TRUE, "none"
    ),
    SWITCH(key,
        "Fixed Effects", Fixed_Effects_Column(),
        "Cluster", "n/a — Cluster grouping RESERVED — v2.6+",
        "none"
    )
))
functions.yields: The grouping-key column for serial-correlation diagnostics: the Fixed Effects data column when a Role="Fixed Effects" row is declared; the token "n/a — Cluster grouping RESERVED — v2.6+" when only a Cluster role is declared; the sentinel "none" when no grouping role exists (ordinary DW path).
functions.description:
Serial_Correlation_Group is the grouping-key resolver for the serial-correlation diagnostics: it answers "which dimension partitions the residuals for within-group differencing?" as a single dispatch point, so consumers (the BFN panel Durbin-Watson wiring) never reference a role column directly. Today the answer is the Fixed Effects column; when the v2.6+ Cluster role supplies pooled-panel grouping without absorption, ONLY this resolver changes — every consumer retargets for free.

The SWITCH dispatches on the declared grouping role, highest-priority first: a Role="Fixed Effects" row wins and returns Fixed_Effects_Column() (one source of truth for the FE lookup — the resolver dispatches, the accessor looks up); a Role="Cluster" row with no FE returns the not-applicable token "n/a — Cluster grouping RESERVED — v2.6+" — the branch is present in the SWITCH but deliberately inert, the switch that currently does nothing, mirroring the reserved-spec-column pattern (Order/Transform columns named now, read by nothing); with neither role the default returns the none-sentinel "none", signalling the ordinary single-series DW path. The Cluster branch is dormant AND unreachable from the shipped cells: "Cluster" is not in the Role dropdown, and the diagnostic cells gate on the FE-variable count before this resolver is ever evaluated — a hand-typed Cluster role reaches the token path, never an error.

Both non-column results are explicit text tokens, not NA() (reserved for genuine errors) — friendlier to a future Model-Comparison XLOOKUP and self-explaining in the audit trail. Spec_Role is TAKE-trimmed to COLUMNS(Source_Data) so cells below the live spec rows are never scanned.
functions.plain_language_summary: Which column groups the residuals for the serial-correlation checks — the Fixed Effects variable today, with a reserved slot for the future Cluster role.
functions.notes: Grouping-key resolver for serial-correlation diagnostics: the FE group column when Role="Fixed Effects" is declared; "n/a — Cluster grouping RESERVED — v2.6+" on a declared Cluster role (dormant branch); "none" otherwise (ordinary DW path).

functions.name: Sequence_Deltas
functions.formula_display:
=LAMBDA(
    LET(
        n_c,     COLUMNS(Source_Data),
        s_pos,   XMATCH(TRUE, TAKE(Spec_Sequence, n_c), 0),
        t_raw,   INDEX(Source_Data, 0, s_pos),
        t_v,     IF(t_raw = "", "", t_raw),
        rl,      TAKE(Spec_Role, n_c),
        id_mask, (rl = "Identifier (Row Label)") * (SEQUENCE(n_c) <> s_pos),
        g_v,     IF(SUM(id_mask) = 0,
            EXPAND("(all)", ROWS(t_v), 1, "(all)"),
            BYROW(CHOOSECOLS(Source_Data, TOROW(FILTER(SEQUENCE(n_c), id_mask))),
                LAMBDA(r, TEXTJOIN(CHAR(31), FALSE, IF(r = "", "", r))))),
        ok,      ISNUMBER(t_v) * (SUBSTITUTE(g_v, CHAR(31), "") <> ""),
        g_f,     FILTER(g_v, ok, NA()),
        t_f,     FILTER(t_v, ok, NA()),
        g_s,     SORTBY(g_f, g_f, 1, t_f, 1),
        t_s,     SORTBY(t_f, g_f, 1, t_f, 1),
        d,       DROP(t_s, 1) - DROP(t_s, -1),
        same,    DROP(g_s, 1) = DROP(g_s, -1),
        IFERROR(FILTER(d, same * (d > 0), NA()), NA())
    )
)
functions.yields: Column of all within-group consecutive positive spacings of the Sequence-flagged column (the raw material of the delta spectrum); #N/A when no Sequence axis is flagged or no group has two observations.
functions.description:
Sequence_Deltas returns every within-group consecutive spacing of the sequence axis: for each group, the differences between successive observed values of the Sequence-flagged column, pooled across groups into one column. It is the raw material for the Base Period Δ candidate (its MODE) and the delta spectrum display.

Seam-safety is the point of the implementation: rows are sorted by (group, seq) and consecutive diffs are kept only where the sorted neighbors share a group, so group seams can never contaminate the spacings. A pooled column-wise diff over the raw row order is forbidden — on Country/Year panel data it would manufacture large negative seam deltas at every country boundary. Zero spacings (duplicate (group, seq) pairs) are also dropped: the spectrum describes the time grid, and duplicates are a data defect surfaced elsewhere.

Groups are keyed by the Identifier-role columns, excluding the sequence column itself (a Year flagged as both Identifier and Sequence must not group by itself), joined with CHAR(31) when there are several. With no Identifier columns the whole sample is one group. A row whose Identifier fields are ALL blank produces a delimiter-only join key, which the emptiness check strips (SUBSTITUTE off the CHAR(31) separators) so unidentified rows never form a spurious group. The spectrum deliberately ignores Sample_Include(): the time grid is dataset structure, while the mask is model-iteration state — a filtered model must not make the data look gappier than it is.

All spec-band reads are TAKE-trimmed to COLUMNS(Source_Data), so the Sequence Spacing block below the spec rows is never scanned.
functions.plain_language_summary: All the observed gaps between consecutive time periods within each group — e.g. all 1s for a complete yearly panel, with a 2 appearing where a year is missing.
functions.notes: Within-group consecutive spacings of the Sequence-flagged column, seam-safe (sorted per group; seams and duplicates dropped). Feeds the Base Period Δ candidate (MODE) and the delta spectrum. #N/A when no axis is flagged.

functions.name: Base_Period_Delta_Candidate
functions.yields: The computed Base Period Δ candidate: MODE of the within-group spacings, falling back to their MIN when no spacing repeats; #N/A when there are no spacings at all.
functions.description:
Base_Period_Delta_Candidate computes the natural base period of the declared sequence axis: the MODE.SNGL of Sequence_Deltas() — the most common within-group consecutive spacing. For a complete yearly panel that is 1; for a decadal survey it is 10. The build writes this candidate into spec cell J (Period In Use) of the Sequence-flagged row; cell I (Sequence Period) is the user-typed override input, and a non-blank I replaces the formula via the reference-level pattern.

When MODE.SNGL returns #N/A because every spacing is distinct, there is no natural base period; the candidate falls back to the MIN of the positive spacings (the finest grid the data could support) and the Sequence Spacing block surfaces an explicit override prompt ("no repeated spacing — set Δ"). When there are no within-group spacings at all — no sequence axis flagged, or every group has a single observation — the candidate is #N/A and cell J displays blank, awaiting a typed Δ in I.

The candidate never quantizes calendar spacings: monthly serial dates produce a spectrum clustered at 28–31 and a MODE of 31, which is a wrong Δ for eleven months of the year. That situation is surfaced (calendar-signature guidance recommending an integer period index upstream), not papered over with a scalar.
functions.plain_language_summary: The suggested time step for the data — the most common gap between consecutive periods within a group (1 for yearly data).
functions.notes: Computed Base Period Δ candidate: MODE.SNGL of Sequence_Deltas(), MIN fallback when no spacing repeats. Pre-fills spec cell J (Period In Use); cell I (Sequence Period) is the override input.

functions.name: Sequence_Delta_Spectrum
functions.formula_display:
=LAMBDA(
    LET(
        d, Sequence_Deltas(),
        u, SORT(UNIQUE(d)),
        IF(COUNT(d) = 0, NA(), HSTACK(u, BYROW(u, LAMBDA(v, SUM(--(d = v))))))
    )
)
functions.yields: Two-column array — each distinct within-group spacing with its count, ascending (the delta spectrum); #N/A when there are no spacings.
functions.description:
Sequence_Delta_Spectrum tabulates the delta spectrum: every distinct within-group consecutive spacing of the sequence axis alongside how many times it occurs, sorted ascending. It is the display behind the Sequence Spacing block's Delta/Count table and the evidence base for its verdict flags.

Reading it: a complete yearly panel shows the single row {1, n−G}. A punched-out year adds a {2, 1} row — the Regularity flag fires, but 2 is still on the Δ = 1 grid so the Off-grid flag stays quiet. First-of-month calendar serials show the signature cluster {28, 29, 30, 31} — Regularity and Off-grid both fire and the calendar-signature guidance recommends an integer period index (YEAR, or YEAR*12 + MONTH) upstream instead of quantizing day counts to a scalar Δ.

Returns #N/A when there are no within-group spacings (no Sequence axis flagged, or every group is a single observation); the consuming cells wrap IFERROR to degrade to a quiet blank.
functions.plain_language_summary: A little table of every gap size found between consecutive time periods and how often each occurs — all 1s means an evenly spaced panel.
functions.notes: The delta spectrum: distinct within-group spacings of the sequence axis with counts, ascending. Drives the Sequence Spacing block's Delta/Count display and verdict flags. #N/A when no spacings exist.

regression_sheet_notes.Pearson R: Measures the straight-line relationship between a predictor and Y. Values near 1 or -1 mean a strong linear relationship; values near 0 mean little linear pattern.
regression_sheet_notes.Spearman R: Measures whether higher X tends to go with higher or lower Y after converting both to ranks. It is useful when the relationship is ordered but curved instead of perfectly linear.
regression_sheet_notes.Skewness: Shows whether the data have a longer tail on one side. Positive means a longer right tail; negative means a longer left tail.
regression_sheet_notes.Kurtosis: Shows how heavy the tails are relative to a normal bell curve. Positive values mean heavier tails with more frequent extremes; values near 0 match a normal distribution.
regression_sheet_notes.GVIF: A measure of collinearity with the other predictors, generalized so a categorical predictor's whole dummy block shares one value instead of a separate number per level. A value of 1 means no overlap; above 5 warrants review, above 10 indicates a problem — those thresholds are exact for a continuous predictor, and reflect the combined block for a multi-level categorical one.
regression_sheet_notes.Tolerance: The fraction of a predictor's variation not explained by the other predictors (1/GVIF) — generalized the same way, so a categorical predictor's dummy columns share one value. Values below 0.2 warrant review; below 0.1 indicate strong collinearity.
regression_sheet_notes.Multiple R: How closely the model's predicted Y values track the actual Y values overall.
regression_sheet_notes.R Square: The share of the outcome's variation explained by the model.
regression_sheet_notes.Adjusted R Square: R Square with a penalty for adding predictors that do not help enough.
regression_sheet_notes.Standard Error: The typical size of the model's prediction errors, measured in the same units as Y.
regression_sheet_notes.Observations: The number of rows actually used in the regression after filtering.
regression_sheet_notes.PRESS: A leave-one-out prediction error score. Lower is better because it means the model predicts unseen rows more accurately.
regression_sheet_notes.PRESS R²: An out-of-sample version of R Square based on leave-one-out prediction. Negative values mean the model predicts worse than just using the average Y.
regression_sheet_notes.Mean Leverage: The average influence each row exerts on the fitted line based on how far it sits from the center of the predictor space. Rows above 2× or 3× this value are flagged by the conditional formatting.
regression_sheet_notes.AIC: A model-comparison score that balances fit against complexity. Lower is better when comparing models on the same data.
regression_sheet_notes.BIC: Another model-comparison score like AIC, but it penalizes extra predictors more strongly.
regression_sheet_notes.AICc: AIC with an extra correction for small samples.
regression_sheet_notes.QQ Correlation: A numeric check of how close the residuals are to a normal bell shape. Values closer to 1 are better.
regression_sheet_notes.Durbin-Watson: A check for serial correlation — whether residuals next to each other in the declared Sequence order tend to move together. Values near 2 mean no autocorrelation; below ~1.5 suggests positive, above ~2.5 negative. Requires exactly one Sequence axis to be flagged; with none the cell reads 'n/a — requires Sequence' (plain row order is not a meaningful time axis), and with two or more it reads 'n/a — multiple Sequence flags' (the spec error the status line above column H reports). With a Fixed Effects variable declared it reads 'n/a — FE active': the single-series statistic is invalid on within-demeaned panel residuals, and the BFN Panel Durbin-Watson cell below takes over.
regression_sheet_notes.BFN Panel Durbin-Watson: The panel (fixed-effects) form of the serial-correlation check, after Bhargava–Franzini–Narendranathan (1982): residual changes are measured within each panel unit only, never across the boundary between two units, so group seams cannot fake a correlation. Read it like Durbin-Watson — near 2 means no first-order autocorrelation in the within residuals — but do NOT judge it against the standard Durbin-Watson significance bounds: BFN has its own critical values that depend on the number of units (N) and periods (T). Surfacing those bounds here is a recorded open item. Active only when both a Sequence axis and a Fixed Effects variable are declared; otherwise the cell shows which ingredient is missing.
regression_sheet_notes.Alpha: The cutoff for statistical significance. At 0.05, results with p-values below 0.05 are treated as statistically significant.
regression_sheet_notes.df: The number of independent data points available to estimate each part of the model — total rows minus one for each estimated parameter.
regression_sheet_notes.SS: The total variation attributed to that source — regression, residual, or total. The raw material from which MS and F are calculated.
regression_sheet_notes.MS: Sum of squares averaged over its degrees of freedom — a per-unit measure of variation for that source.
regression_sheet_notes.F: The model-vs-noise ratio used in the overall regression significance test.
regression_sheet_notes.Significance F: The p-value for the overall F test. Small values mean the model as a whole is unlikely to be pure noise.
regression_sheet_notes.Regression: The variation explained by the predictors taken together.
regression_sheet_notes.Residual: The variation the model does not explain.
regression_sheet_notes.Total: All variation in the outcome before splitting it into explained and unexplained parts.
regression_sheet_notes.Coefficients: The fitted weights used to turn predictor values into predictions.
regression_sheet_notes.Std Error: How uncertain each coefficient estimate is.
regression_sheet_notes.t Stat: How many standard errors the coefficient is away from zero.
regression_sheet_notes.P-value: How surprising this coefficient would be if its true effect were zero. Smaller values mean stronger evidence of a real effect.
regression_sheet_notes.Lower 95%: The lower bound of the 95% confidence interval.
regression_sheet_notes.Upper 95%: The upper bound of the 95% confidence interval.
regression_sheet_notes.Beta Weight: The coefficient after standardizing units, so predictors can be compared on the same scale.
regression_sheet_notes.Point Estimate: The model's single best predicted Y value for the inputs you entered.
regression_sheet_notes.SE Prediction: The standard error for a new prediction. It reflects both model uncertainty and ordinary row-to-row noise.
regression_sheet_notes.t Critical: The t-distribution cutoff at the chosen confidence level. Multiply by SE Prediction to get the prediction interval half-width.
regression_sheet_notes.Confidence Level: The probability level associated with the interval. With alpha 0.05, this is 95%.
regression_sheet_notes.Predicted Y: The fitted outcome values produced by the model.
regression_sheet_notes.Residuals: Actual Y minus predicted Y. Positive means the row came in above the model's prediction; negative means below.
regression_sheet_notes.Hat Diagonal: Leverage. It shows how unusual a row's predictor values are relative to the rest of the data.
regression_sheet_notes.Studentized Residuals: Residuals scaled to account for overall error size and leverage, making outliers easier to compare fairly.
regression_sheet_notes.Cook's Distance: How much a single row can pull the fitted coefficients and predictions around.
regression_sheet_notes.Normal Scores Ranked: Expected bell-curve quantiles used for the Q-Q comparison.
regression_sheet_notes.Studentized Residuals Ranked: Studentized residuals sorted from smallest to largest for the Q-Q plot.
regression_sheet_notes.Scale-Location: The square root of the absolute studentized residual. A flat pattern suggests stable error spread.
regression_sheet_notes.PRESS Residual: The prediction error for a row when that row is left out of the fitting step (the leave-one-out / LOOCV residual). Summing its squares gives PRESS.
